texto:
A community garden is a special place where people from a neighborhood work together to grow plants. Instead of having a private garden at home, they share a large piece of land. Last year, our town started a new community garden near the park. Many families joined, and it was a big success. Everyone gets a small part of the garden to plant what they like. Some people grow colorful flowers, while others prefer to grow fresh vegetables like tomatoes, carrots, and lettuce.

The garden is more than just a place to grow food. It is also a place where neighbors meet and talk. Children learn where their food comes from, and adults share tips about gardening. At the end of the summer, everyone shares the food they grew. This helps people eat healthy, fresh food and it also builds a stronger community. It’s a wonderful project for any town.

preguntas.pregunta: According to the text, what do people grow in the community garden?
preguntas.explicacion: La respuesta correcta es B porque el texto dice explícitamente que la gente cultiva flores y vegetales. The text states: 'Some people grow colorful flowers, while others prefer to grow fresh vegetables like tomatoes, carrots, and lettuce'. Las otras opciones son incorrectas. A es incorrecta porque el texto no menciona 'fruit trees'. C es incorrecta porque no se mencionan hierbas ('herbs'). D menciona vegetales específicos ('corn and potatoes') que no están en la lista del texto. E es incorrecta porque el propósito principal es cultivar plantas, no solo reunirse.

preguntas.pregunta: From the text, we can infer that an important benefit of the community garden is that it...

opciones.A: helps people save a lot of money on food.
opciones.B: allows people to sell vegetables at the local market.
opciones.E: is open only during the summer season.

preguntas.explicacion: La respuesta correcta es C. Aunque el texto no lo dice directamente con esas palabras, podemos inferirlo. The text mentions that the garden is 'a place where neighbors meet and talk' y que 'it also builds a stronger community'. Esto sugiere que mejorar las conexiones sociales es un beneficio clave. Las otras opciones no se pueden deducir. A (ahorrar dinero) no es la idea principal. B (vender los vegetales) no se menciona; de hecho, se dice que los comparten ('everyone shares the food'). D es incorrecta porque el texto sugiere que los principiantes pueden aprender ('adults share tips'). E es incorrecta porque no se especifica que solo abra en verano.
